name: AWS security findings
description: Finding-shaped output from AWS's three security-finding services: GuardDuty (threat detection), Inspector v2 (vulnerability scanning) and IAM Access Analyzer (external and unused access), as the Splunk Add-on for AWS ingests each.
source: AWS API and EventBridge schema documentation for GuardDuty, Inspector v2 and IAM Access Analyzer; Splunk Add-on for AWS field aliases and lookups, checked against a live instance and captured findings.

feed.label: AWS security findings
feed.description: Security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector v2 and IAM Access Analyzer: what was found, on which resource, how severe, and its current status.

aws_account_id.label: AWS account id
aws_account_id.description: The AWS account this finding or the resource it is about belongs to.

aws_region.label: AWS region
aws_region.description: The AWS region the finding or the resource it is about is in.

gd_envelope_event_id.label: EventBridge envelope event id
gd_envelope_event_id.description: The id EventBridge assigned to the delivery envelope, a dashed UUID. Only present where the envelope is not stripped (aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty); distinct from the finding's own id.

gd_envelope_meta.label: EventBridge envelope metadata
gd_envelope_meta.description: The envelope's own version, detail-type and source keys ("GuardDuty Finding", "aws.guardduty"), constant for every GuardDuty finding delivered through EventBridge.

gd_finding_id.label: Finding id
gd_finding_id.description: GuardDuty's own id for this finding, a 32-character hex string. Stable across updates to the same finding (GuardDuty aggregates repeat activity into the same finding id).

gd_detector_id.label: Detector id
gd_detector_id.description: The id of the GuardDuty detector (one per account per region) that raised this finding, a 32-character hex string in the same shape as a finding id but a different value.

gd_schema_version.label: Finding schema version
gd_schema_version.description: Version of the GuardDuty finding JSON schema (e.g. 2.0).

gd_partition.label: AWS partition
gd_partition.description: The AWS partition the finding's resources live in (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov).

gd_finding_type.label: Finding type
gd_finding_type.description: GuardDuty's finding type string, a colon- and slash-structured name: ThreatPurpose:ResourceTypeAffected/ThreatFamilyName, with an optional .DetectionMechanism and !Artifact suffix (for example UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/SSHBruteForce, or CryptoCurrency:EC2/BitcoinTool.B!DNS). ThreatPurpose is the primary purpose or attack stage; ResourceTypeAffected is the AWS resource type the finding targets; ThreatFamilyName names the overall activity; DetectionMechanism marks a detection variant (for example .Custom on a custom threat list, .Reputation on a domain reputation model); Artifact names a tool-owned resource, when GuardDuty reports one. The finding-format page lists these ThreatPurpose values: Backdoor (a compromised resource altered so it can reach a command-and-control server); Behavior (activity that departs from the resource's established baseline); CredentialAccess (an attempt to steal passwords, usernames or access keys); Cryptocurrency (a resource hosting cryptocurrency-related software); DefenseEvasion (an attempt to avoid detection while infiltrating the environment); Discovery (an attempt to map out your systems and internal networks); Execution (malicious code run or attempted, to explore the environment or steal data); Exfiltration (an attempt to steal data out of the environment); Impact (an attempt to manipulate, interrupt or destroy systems and data); InitialAccess (the stage where an adversary is establishing a foothold); Pentest (activity resembling a known penetration-testing tool, authorized or not); Persistence (an attempt to keep access after the original route is cut off); Policy (behavior against recommended security practice, for example an over-permissive change); PrivilegeEscalation (an attempt to gain higher-level permissions); Recon (reconnaissance: port probes, API calls, listing users or tables); Stealth (an adversary actively hiding their actions, for example behind an anonymizing proxy); Trojan (malicious activity carried out by software disguised as legitimate); UnauthorizedAccess (suspicious activity by an unauthorized individual). Attack-sequence findings use AttackSequence in the same slot for a correlated chain of signals; that value is not in the page's ThreatPurpose list. The values dictionary for this concept enumerates every active finding type GuardDuty documents, by resource.

gd_finding_category.label: Finding category (TA)
gd_finding_category.description: The Splunk Add-on for AWS's own category bucket for the finding type, from its bundled aws_cloudwatch_guardduty_category_750.csv lookup (about 750 finding types mapped to a category). Not an AWS-published field.

gd_severity.label: Severity score
gd_severity.description: Numeric severity GuardDuty assigns the finding, 1.0-10.0; higher is more severe.

gd_severity_id.label: Severity bucket (TA)
gd_severity_id.description: The Splunk Add-on for AWS's own bucket for the numeric severity (e.g. low/medium/high), computed from detail.severity. Not an AWS-published field; the TA's exact lookup was not read, so the bucket boundaries here are inferred from AWS's own documented Critical/High/Medium/Low ranges, not confirmed against the TA's lookup file.

gd_title.label: Finding title
gd_title.description: A one-line, human-readable summary of the finding, usually the same string as the finding type.

gd_description.label: Finding description
gd_description.description: A longer human-readable description of the finding.

gd_created_at.label: Finding created at
gd_created_at.description: When GuardDuty first created this finding record.

gd_updated_at.label: Finding updated at
gd_updated_at.description: When GuardDuty last updated this finding (GuardDuty aggregates repeat activity into the same finding rather than creating a new one).

gd_event_first_seen.label: Activity first seen
gd_event_first_seen.description: When the underlying activity behind this finding was first observed, independent of when the finding record was created or updated.

gd_event_last_seen.label: Activity last seen
gd_event_last_seen.description: When the underlying activity behind this finding was most recently observed.

gd_envelope_time.label: Envelope dispatch time
gd_envelope_time.description: The EventBridge envelope's own time key: when EventBridge dispatched this delivery, not when the finding happened. On aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty this is also the only field the TA's props could ever key a real event time from, and the TA does not key on it (see hazard).

gd_service_name.label: GuardDuty service name
gd_service_name.description: Constant "guardduty": which AWS service raised the finding.

gd_resource_role.label: Resource role
gd_resource_role.description: Whether the named resource was the ACTOR (initiated the activity) or the TARGET (was acted upon).

gd_archived.label: Archived
gd_archived.description: Whether the finding has been archived in the GuardDuty console/API.

gd_occurrence_count.label: Occurrence count
gd_occurrence_count.description: How many times GuardDuty has observed this same activity and folded it into this finding.

gd_action_type.label: Action type
gd_action_type.description: Which kind of activity this finding's service.action object describes (which of its sibling *Action objects is populated): AWS_API_CALL, DNS_REQUEST, KUBERNETES_API_CALL, NETWORK_CONNECTION, PORT_PROBE or RDS_LOGIN_ATTEMPT.

gd_connection_direction.label: Connection direction
gd_connection_direction.description: Direction of the network connection the finding describes, relative to the resource.

gd_protocol.label: Network protocol
gd_protocol.description: Transport protocol of the network connection (e.g. TCP, UDP).

gd_blocked.label: Connection blocked
gd_blocked.description: Whether EC2 blocked the network connection.

gd_local_port.label: Local port
gd_local_port.description: Local port number of the network connection.

gd_local_port_name.label: Local port name
gd_local_port_name.description: The well-known service name GuardDuty resolved for the local port (e.g. SSH), or Unknown.

gd_remote_port.label: Remote port
gd_remote_port.description: Remote port number of the network connection.

gd_remote_port_name.label: Remote port name
gd_remote_port_name.description: The well-known service name GuardDuty resolved for the remote port (e.g. SSH).

gd_remote_ip.label: Remote IP address
gd_remote_ip.description: The IPv4 address at the other end of the connection or API call GuardDuty analyzed.

gd_remote_geo.label: Remote IP enrichment
gd_remote_geo.description: GuardDuty's IP-intelligence enrichment of the remote address: city, country, lat/lon, ASN, ISP and organization name. Best-effort geolocation, not authoritative.

gd_api_call_detail.label: AWS API call detail
gd_api_call_detail.description: For an AWS_API_CALL action, which API was called, the caller type, the error code (if any) and the service name.

gd_additional_info.label: Additional info
gd_additional_info.description: Service-specific extra context GuardDuty attaches to some finding types (older findings: a matched threat-list name and the unusual port/protocol; newer findings: a generic sample/type/value triple).

gd_instance_id.label: EC2 instance id
gd_instance_id.description: The EC2 instance id the finding is about.

gd_instance_state.label: EC2 instance state
gd_instance_state.description: The instance's state at the time of the finding (e.g. running).

gd_instance_platform.label: EC2 instance platform
gd_instance_platform.description: The instance's operating system platform, when GuardDuty reports one.

gd_image_id.label: AMI id
gd_image_id.description: The AMI id the instance was launched from.

gd_image_description.label: AMI description
gd_image_description.description: The human-readable description of the AMI.

gd_launch_time.label: Instance launch time
gd_launch_time.description: When the EC2 instance was launched. A raw epoch-milliseconds number, not an ISO 8601 string (see hazard).

gd_subnet_id.label: Subnet id
gd_subnet_id.description: The VPC subnet id of the instance's network interface.

gd_vpc_id.label: VPC id
gd_vpc_id.description: The VPC id of the instance's network interface.

gd_private_ip.label: Private IP address
gd_private_ip.description: A private IPv4 address of the instance's network interface (primary or a secondary address on the same interface).

gd_private_dns.label: Private DNS name
gd_private_dns.description: The private DNS name matching a private IP address of the instance.

gd_public_ip.label: Public IP address
gd_public_ip.description: The public IPv4 address of the instance's network interface, when it has one.

gd_public_dns.label: Public DNS name
gd_public_dns.description: The public DNS name of the instance's network interface, when it has one.

gd_security_group_id.label: Security group id
gd_security_group_id.description: A security group id attached to the instance's network interface.

gd_security_group_name.label: Security group name
gd_security_group_name.description: The human-assigned name of a security group attached to the instance.

gd_resource_tag_key.label: Resource tag key
gd_resource_tag_key.description: The key of an AWS tag on the resource.

gd_resource_tag_value.label: Resource tag value
gd_resource_tag_value.description: The value of an AWS tag on the resource.

gd_instance_iam_profile.label: Instance IAM profile
gd_instance_iam_profile.description: The ARN and id of the IAM instance profile attached to the instance, when there is one.

gd_resource_type.label: Resource type
gd_resource_type.description: The kind of AWS resource this finding is about (Instance, AccessKey, S3Bucket and others GuardDuty defines). AWS documents the containing object but not a closed enum of literal values.

gd_access_key_id.label: Access key id
gd_access_key_id.description: The IAM access key id involved in the finding, for AccessKey-type findings.

gd_principal_id.label: Principal id
gd_principal_id.description: The principal id of the IAM user or role whose credentials are involved.

gd_user_name.label: User name
gd_user_name.description: The IAM user name associated with the finding.

gd_access_key_user_type.label: Access key user type
gd_access_key_user_type.description: The type of principal that owns the access key involved (e.g. IAMUser, AssumedRole, Root). Not confirmed against a sample; no AccessKey-type finding is in this pack's sample set.
gd_access_key_user_type.notes: Column is in the observed set but no sample event of this finding shape backs an example; the enum vocabulary is inferred by analogy with CloudTrail's userIdentity.type, not read from a GuardDuty source.

gd_s3_bucket_arn.label: S3 bucket ARN
gd_s3_bucket_arn.description: The ARN of the S3 bucket the finding is about.

gd_s3_bucket_name.label: S3 bucket name
gd_s3_bucket_name.description: The name of the S3 bucket the finding is about.

gd_s3_bucket_owner.label: S3 bucket owner id
gd_s3_bucket_owner.description: The account id that owns the S3 bucket.

gd_s3_bucket_created_at.label: S3 bucket created at
gd_s3_bucket_created_at.description: When the S3 bucket was created.

gd_s3_bucket_type.label: S3 bucket type
gd_s3_bucket_type.description: GuardDuty's classification of the bucket (e.g. Destination, Source).

gd_s3_bucket_encryption.label: S3 bucket default encryption
gd_s3_bucket_encryption.description: The bucket's default server-side encryption type and, if SSE-KMS, the key ARN.

gd_s3_public_access.label: S3 bucket public access
gd_s3_public_access.description: GuardDuty's rollup of the bucket's public-access posture: the effective permission and every contributing account-level and bucket-level Block Public Access, ACL and bucket-policy setting.

insp_finding_type.label: Finding type
insp_finding_type.description: Which kind of finding this is: NETWORK_REACHABILITY, PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY or CODE_VULNERABILITY. Decides which other fields the finding carries.

insp_title.label: Finding title
insp_title.description: A one-line summary of the finding, usually the CVE id and package name.

insp_description.label: Finding description
insp_description.description: A longer description of the vulnerability.

insp_severity.label: Severity
insp_severity.description: Inspector's severity rating for the finding.

insp_first_observed_at.label: First observed at
insp_first_observed_at.description: When Inspector first observed this finding. A ctime-style string, not ISO 8601 (see hazard).

insp_last_observed_at.label: Last observed at
insp_last_observed_at.description: When Inspector most recently observed this finding; unchanged until the finding is updated. A ctime-style string, not ISO 8601. This pack's sample entry uses it as the record's time field.

insp_updated_at.label: Updated at
insp_updated_at.description: When the finding was last updated. A ctime-style string, not ISO 8601.

insp_inspector_score.label: Inspector score
insp_inspector_score.description: Inspector's own numeric score for the finding, which can differ from the vendor CVSS base score once Inspector's contextual adjustments are applied.

insp_inspector_score_details.label: Inspector score adjustment detail
insp_inspector_score_details.description: The adjusted CVSS score, its source, scoring vector and version, and any adjustments Inspector applied to the vendor score.

insp_exploit_available.label: Exploit available
insp_exploit_available.description: Whether an exploit is known to be available for the vulnerability.

insp_fix_available.label: Fix available
insp_fix_available.description: Whether a fix is available through a package/version update.

insp_epss_score.label: EPSS score
insp_epss_score.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System probability (0-1) that this vulnerability will be exploited in the wild in the next 30 days.

insp_cve_id.label: CVE id
insp_cve_id.description: The CVE identifier for the vulnerability (from packageVulnerabilityDetails.vulnerabilityId, surfaced by the TA as a top-level cve field).

insp_vulnerability_source.label: Vulnerability source
insp_vulnerability_source.description: Which vulnerability database Inspector sourced this finding from (e.g. UBUNTU_CVE, NVD).

insp_vulnerability_source_url.label: Vulnerability source URL
insp_vulnerability_source_url.description: URL of the source vulnerability advisory.

insp_vendor_severity.label: Vendor severity
insp_vendor_severity.description: The severity the upstream vulnerability database assigned, independent of Inspector's own score.

insp_vendor_created_at.label: Vendor created at
insp_vendor_created_at.description: When the upstream vulnerability database published the advisory. A ctime-style string, not ISO 8601.

insp_cvss.label: CVSS score entry
insp_cvss.description: One CVSS scoring entry (base score, scoring vector, version and which source computed it); a finding can carry more than one, from different sources.

insp_reference_urls.label: Reference URLs
insp_reference_urls.description: External reference URLs for the vulnerability.

insp_related_vulnerabilities.label: Related vulnerabilities
insp_related_vulnerabilities.description: Other vulnerability/advisory ids related to this one (e.g. a distro's own USN id).

insp_package_name.label: Vulnerable package name
insp_package_name.description: Name of the vulnerable software package.

insp_package_version.label: Vulnerable package version
insp_package_version.description: The installed version of the vulnerable package.

insp_package_fixed_version.label: Fixed package version
insp_package_fixed_version.description: The package version that fixes the vulnerability, when known.

insp_package_manager.label: Package manager
insp_package_manager.description: Which package manager reported the package (e.g. OS for the distro's own package manager).

insp_package_arch.label: Package architecture
insp_package_arch.description: CPU architecture of the vulnerable package build.

insp_resource_id.label: Affected resource id
insp_resource_id.description: The id of the AWS or non-AWS resource the finding is about (an EC2 instance id, an ECR image digest, a Lambda ARN...).

insp_resource_type.label: Affected resource type
insp_resource_type.description: Inspector's type tag for the affected resource (e.g. AWS_EC2_INSTANCE).

insp_resource_region.label: Resource region
insp_resource_region.description: The region of the affected resource, which can differ from the finding's own account-level region on a cross-region scan.

insp_instance_ip.label: Instance IP address
insp_instance_ip.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address of the affected EC2 instance.

insp_instance_platform.label: Instance platform
insp_instance_platform.description: The affected instance's OS platform (e.g. UBUNTU_22_04).

insp_instance_launched_at.label: Instance launched at
insp_instance_launched_at.description: When the affected instance was launched. A ctime-style string, not ISO 8601.

insp_instance_subnet_id.label: Instance subnet id
insp_instance_subnet_id.description: The VPC subnet id of the affected instance.

insp_instance_vpc_id.label: Instance VPC id
insp_instance_vpc_id.description: The VPC id of the affected instance.

insp_instance_iam_profile.label: Instance IAM profile ARN
insp_instance_iam_profile.description: The IAM instance profile ARN attached to the affected instance.

insp_instance_image_id.label: Instance AMI id
insp_instance_image_id.description: The AMI id the affected instance was launched from.

aa_finding_id.label: Finding id
aa_finding_id.description: Access Analyzer's own id for this finding (a UUID under detail.id/detail.findingId; the envelope's own id is a separate, unrelated UUID, see hazard).

aa_finding_type.label: Finding type
aa_finding_type.description: Which kind of Access Analyzer finding this is (InternalAccess, UnusedPermission and the other unused-access/external-access types EventBridge's detail-type also names). Decides which other detail fields are present.

aa_previous_status.label: Previous status
aa_previous_status.description: The finding's status before this update, when the finding was updated rather than newly created.

aa_is_deleted.label: Finding deleted
aa_is_deleted.description: Whether the finding has been deleted (the analyzed resource or access no longer exists).

aa_created_at.label: Finding created at
aa_created_at.description: When Access Analyzer generated the finding.

aa_updated_at.label: Finding updated at
aa_updated_at.description: When the finding was last updated.

aa_analyzed_at.label: Resource analyzed at
aa_analyzed_at.description: When Access Analyzer last analyzed the resource or access pattern behind this finding.

aa_account_owner.label: Principal owner account
aa_account_owner.description: The AWS account that owns the external principal named in the finding.

aa_resource.label: Resource
aa_resource.description: The ARN of the resource the finding is about.

aa_resource_type.label: Resource type
aa_resource_type.description: The CloudFormation-style type of the analyzed resource.

aa_principal.label: External principal
aa_principal.description: The external AWS principal (account, role, user or service) that has the access described by the finding, for an external-access finding.

aa_principal_type.label: Principal type
aa_principal_type.description: The kind of the external principal (e.g. IAM_ROLE, AWS_ACCOUNT, AWS_SERVICE).

aa_access_type.label: Access type
aa_access_type.description: Whether the access described crosses accounts or stays within one (e.g. INTRA_ACCOUNT).

aa_action.label: Granted actions
aa_action.description: The API action(s) the analyzed policy statement grants the external principal.

aa_rcp_restriction.label: Resource control policy restriction
aa_rcp_restriction.description: Whether an Organizations resource control policy (RCP) applies to and restricts this finding's access.

aa_scp_restriction.label: Service control policy restriction
aa_scp_restriction.description: Whether an Organizations service control policy (SCP) applies to and restricts this finding's access. No AWS page documents this field's own enum separately from the RCP one; only its observed value is recorded here.
aa_scp_restriction.notes: Same NOT_APPLICABLE literal observed as resourceControlPolicyRestrictionType; no separate API page for the SCP field was found, so its full enum is not asserted, only what the sample shows.

aa_unused_services_count.label: Unused services count
aa_unused_services_count.description: For an UnusedPermission finding, how many services the principal has never used.

aa_unused_actions_count.label: Unused actions count
aa_unused_actions_count.description: For an UnusedPermission finding, how many granted actions the principal has never used.

aa_finding_version.label: Finding version
aa_finding_version.description: A version marker on the finding record. On an InternalAccess finding this is the finding schema version (e.g. "1.0"); on an UnusedPermission finding the sample shows a UUID instead, so treat the two record types' version field as differently shaped.

sh_schema_version.label: ASFF schema version
sh_schema_version.description: The AWS Security Finding Format version a finding is written to; one fixed value across the whole family (2018-10-08).

sh_product_arn.label: Product ARN
sh_product_arn.description: The ARN of the Security Hub product that generated the finding, arn:{partition}:securityhub:{region}:{account}:product/{company}/{product}.

sh_record_state.label: Record state
sh_record_state.description: Whether Security Hub still shows this finding as current (ACTIVE) or has hidden it (ARCHIVED); set by the finding provider, distinct from the analyst's own Workflow.Status.

sh_workflow_status.label: Workflow status
sh_workflow_status.description: The analyst's own triage state for the finding (NEW, NOTIFIED, SUPPRESSED, RESOLVED), independent of RecordState.

sh_severity_label.label: Severity label
sh_severity_label.description: Security Hub's normalized severity word (INFORMATIONAL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL), assigned from the finding provider's own score.

sh_severity_normalized.label: Severity, normalized
sh_severity_normalized.description: Severity on a 0-100 scale; Security Hub fills this in from Label when the provider gives only one of the two.

sh_source_url.label: Source URL
sh_source_url.description: A link to the finding in the product that generated it (here, the GuardDuty console).

sh_resource_type.label: ASFF resource type
sh_resource_type.description: The affected resource's type in ASFF's own naming (AwsEc2Instance, AwsS3Bucket, AwsIamAccessKey...), not GuardDuty's own resourceType vocabulary.

sh_product_name.label: Product name
sh_product_name.description: The name of the product that generated the finding (GuardDuty, for every event in this dataset).

sh_cim_alert_type.label: CIM alert type (TA)
sh_cim_alert_type.description: A fixed literal the TA writes for this sourcetype's CIM Intrusion Detection type field; not part of the ASFF finding itself.

sh_types.label: Finding types
sh_types.description: One or more {namespace}/{category}/{classifier} paths that classify the finding (for example TTPs/Initial Access/...); AWS defines the namespaces and recommends but doesn't require the rest.

aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty.description: GuardDuty findings delivered through Amazon EventBridge to CloudWatch Logs and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's CloudWatch Logs input. Each event is the full EventBridge envelope (version, id, detail-type, source, account, time, region, resources, detail), with the finding itself nested under detail.
aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty.note: No TIME_PREFIX/TIME_FORMAT is set on this container's own props stanza, so Splunk indexes it at ingest time; see the gd_cwlogs_time_basis hazard.

aws:cloudwatch:guardduty.description: GuardDuty findings delivered through Amazon EventBridge to Kinesis Data Firehose and on to Splunk HEC. The TA's transforms strip the EventBridge envelope at index time (source=aws_cloudwatchevents_guardduty), so the stored event is the bare finding object, the same schema as detail on aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty but with no envelope wrapper and a different set of TA-computed CIM aliases.
aws:cloudwatch:guardduty.note: No sample dataset ships with this pack for this container: AWS publishes only a placeholder-valued envelope example, and a genuine bare finding cannot be timed correctly under this TA's shipped props. Column names below are read from genuine AWS finding bodies observed in the dev index, not from a validated sample.

aws:inspector:v2:findings.description: Amazon Inspector v2 findings, pulled directly by the Splunk Add-on for AWS's Inspector v2 input (inspector2 ListFindings), not through EventBridge. Each event is the raw Finding object with no envelope wrapper.
aws:inspector:v2:findings.note: This pack's sample entry names lastObservedAt as the time field; index_time_ok is false for it.

aws:accessanalyzer:finding.description: AWS IAM Access Analyzer findings (external access and unused access) delivered through Amazon EventBridge and pulled by the Splunk Add-on for AWS. The TA's transform strips the EventBridge envelope at index time (source=aws_eventbridgeevents_iam_aa), so the stored event is the bare finding object; the envelope's own account/region/time/source/detail-type/resources keys are not indexed.
aws:accessanalyzer:finding.note: This pack's sample entry names createdAt as the time field; index_time_ok is false for it.

aws:securityhub:finding.description: AWS Security Hub CSPM findings in AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF), as the Splunk Add-on for AWS ingests them. Every event observed on the dev index is a GuardDuty finding Security Hub has re-published in its own envelope; the raw finding survives under ProductFields.aws/guardduty/service/*, unchanged.
aws:securityhub:finding.note: This container adds no new resource-scanning coverage of its own for this pack (no Inspector- or native-control-sourced event was seen on the dev index): it is GuardDuty's findings under a second, ASFF-shaped skin, plus the workflow/record-state fields ASFF adds on top.

gd_id_lookalike.text: GuardDuty has three same-shaped ids that are not interchangeable: the EventBridge envelope's own id (a dashed UUID, only present when the envelope is not stripped), the finding id (a 32-character hex string, detail.id / bare id after stripping) and the detector id (also 32-character hex). On aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty, bare column id is the envelope's UUID; on aws:cloudwatch:guardduty, bare column id is the finding's own hex id, because that container's pipeline strips the envelope first. The same column name means two different things on the two containers.

gd_cwlogs_time_basis.text: aws:cloudwatchlogs:guardduty is index_time_ok in this pack's own seeding (no TIME_PREFIX/TIME_FORMAT on its props stanza), so _time is when Splunk indexed the event, not when GuardDuty raised the finding. The envelope's own time key also carries a 1970-01-01 placeholder in AWS's published sample and sits past Splunk's default timestamp lookahead in the real wire format either way. Use detail.createdAt, detail.updatedAt or detail.service.eventFirstSeen/eventLastSeen for the finding's real time, never _time, on this container.

gd_launch_time_epoch_ms.text: instanceDetails.launchTime is a raw Unix epoch-milliseconds number (e.g. 1492735675000), unlike every other GuardDuty finding timestamp, which is an ISO 8601 string. Parsing it as a date string silently produces a wrong time.

insp_ctime_format.text: Amazon Inspector's own timestamps (firstObservedAt, lastObservedAt, updatedAt, vendorCreatedAt) are C ctime-style strings, e.g. "Wed Sep 04 16:59:44.356 UTC 2024", not ISO 8601. A parser expecting ISO 8601 (as most of this family's other sourcetypes use) will fail or silently misparse.

gd_cloudwatch_no_sample.text: aws:cloudwatch:guardduty ships no vendor-published sample in this pack: AWS's only public envelope example uses placeholder values, and the TA's props make a bare finding structurally untimeable. Column names here come from genuine AWS finding bodies observed in the dev index, but no single full event or _time value from this container should be treated as a validated example.

sh_id_lookalike.text: aws:securityhub:finding carries three more id-shaped columns on top of the family's existing GuardDuty id hazard: top-level Id (the full finding ARN, shared with gd_finding_arn), CIM id (the TA-extracted bare hex, shared with gd_finding_id) and GeneratorId (the detector's own ARN, shared with gd_detector_id). None are interchangeable; signature_id also carries the detector ARN, not the finding id, despite the CIM name.

sh_two_time_bases.text: CreatedAt/UpdatedAt/FirstObservedAt/LastObservedAt are ASFF's own ISO 8601 timestamps, shared with the equivalent GuardDuty finding columns and confirmed equal to them on the dev index for this dataset. Resources{}.Details.AwsEc2Instance.LaunchedAt is also ISO 8601 here, unlike GuardDuty's own epoch-millisecond instanceDetails.launchTime (gd_launch_time_epoch_ms): ASFF reformats it on the way in.

sh_record_vs_workflow_state.text: RecordState (ACTIVE/ARCHIVED, set by the finding provider) and Workflow.Status (NEW/NOTIFIED/SUPPRESSED/RESOLVED, set by the analyst) both describe a finding's status but answer different questions; AWS's own guidance is to use Workflow for investigation tracking, never RecordState.
